0The three AWS accounts

AWS's account setup created an organization with three accounts. Accounts are free; you pay only for what runs in them.

Management account

The owner's office. Owns the organization, pays one combined bill, holds the credits, and sets rules (SCPs) for every account. Open it only for billing and rules.

Identity delegated admin

The security desk. Runs IAM Identity Center, which gives you the AccountFullAccessRole sign-in on each card. Nothing to do here for this project.

Workload account

The workshop. Everything this project creates lives here. In this setup it is called First Principles. Your AWS CLI and GitHub Actions use it.

Switching between accounts

  1. Open https://console.aws.amazon.com/. The AWS sign-ins page shows one card per account.
  2. Select the account name (already signed in) or Sign in (not yet). This only opens a console session; it changes nothing.
  3. The account you are in is shown at the top right of every console page. Check it before you change anything.

1Payment method (credit card) ONE TIMEManagement account

AWS needs a payment method on the management account; it pays for all three accounts. Credits are used first, and the card is charged only for what credits do not cover.

Check first: open Billing and Cost Management › Payment preferences. If Default payment preferences already shows a card under Payment method, skip this step.
  1. Sign in to the management account.
  2. Type Billing in the console search bar and open Billing and Cost Management.
  3. In the left menu choose Payments, then the Payment preferences page.
  4. Select Add payment method, enter the card yourself on AWS's page, and make it the default.
  5. Optional: under Default payment preferences › Edit you can set the payment currency; this setup left it unset.
Never paste card numbers, the security code, passwords or MFA codes into chat, AI tools, files or screenshots. Type them only into AWS's own page.

2Credits and free tier ONE TIME lookManagement account

This organization has $120 of credits: $100 AWS Free Tier and $20 for setting up a cost budget, both valid until 11/23/2027. They cover Route 53, CloudFront, S3, CloudWatch and SNS, so everything this site uses.

  1. In the management account open Billing and Cost Management › Credits.
  2. Read Total amount used and Available credit. Select a credit's See complete list of services to see what it covers.
  3. Amounts update about once every 24 hours, so a new deployment shows $0.00 at first.

3CloudFront account verification ONE TIMEWorkload account

Our first terraform apply failed with Your account must be verified before you can add new CloudFront resources. This is a hold on the whole account, not one region. Only AWS Support can lift it.

Check first: open Support Center › Support Cases. If a case about account verification is already Resolved, or terraform apply does not show this error, skip this step.
  1. Sign in to the workload account. Type Support in the console search bar, or go to https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/home.
  2. In Describe your issue to get support, explain that you need CloudFront and paste the error text. AWS first answers automatically; select Create a case.
  3. Choose Case type: Account and billing, Service: Account Activation, Category: Account Verification, Severity: General question. These cases are free on the Basic plan.
  4. Subject: Account verification needed to create CloudFront distributions. Submit.
  5. Wait for Resolved in Support Cases before running terraform apply again. Ours took a few hours.

4Region rule: what you can and cannot use ONE TIMEManagement account

The organization has a service control policy (SCP) named AdvancedModeRegionRestrictionSecurityControlPolicy, attached to Root, so it limits every account. No IAM permission can override it. This is why some services "don't work":

RegionWhat is allowed
us-east-2 (Ohio)Everything. No deny applies to this region.
us-east-1 (N. Virginia)Only the exempted list (NotAction in statement UsEast1Partitional): global services such as IAM, CloudFront, Route 53, ACM, STS, Organizations, billing and support, plus what we added: S3, SNS and the alarm actions. Anything else, for example running EC2 instances, Lambda or DynamoDB, is denied there.
us-west-2 (Oregon)A short list: Bedrock model calls, CloudShell, KMS decrypt and describe, Identity Center, Health, Service Quotas, Support, Trusted Advisor, Network Manager and Route 53 recovery.
Every other regionDenied, except Bedrock model calls such as InvokeModel.
Also in the policy list: four BudgetsSpendLimit… SCPs (Bedrock, Lambda, SageMaker, new chargeable resources). They are managed by AWS Budgets and block those services in an account when forecasted spend approaches your spend limit. Today they are not applied to the workload account; the screenshot below shows what is applied.

Why this project needs us-east-1: Route 53 health-check metrics exist only there, so the alarm and its SNS topic must be there too, and we put both buckets there as well. The first apply failed with explicit deny in a service control policy for sns:CreateTopic, and creating a bucket failed the same way for s3:CreateBucket.

Check first: open the policy's Content tab and search the page (Ctrl+F) for "sns:*" and "s3:*". If both, plus the four cloudwatch: actions below, are already in the UsEast1Partitional list, skip this step.
  1. Sign in to the management account. Open AWS Organizations › Policies › Service control policies.
  2. Open AdvancedModeRegionRestrictionSecurityControlPolicy. Its Targets tab shows Root.
  3. On Content, find "Sid": "UsEast1Partitional": a Deny with a NotAction list and aws:RequestedRegion = us-east-1. Every action in that list is allowed in us-east-1.
  4. Back up first: copy the whole JSON into a local file. SCPs keep no history, so this copy is the only way back.
  5. Select Edit policy. In the UsEast1Partitional list only:
    • replace the separate "s3:..." entries with one "s3:*" (both buckets and the deploy upload)
    • add "sns:*" (alert topic and email)
    • add "cloudwatch:PutMetricAlarm", "cloudwatch:DeleteAlarms", "cloudwatch:TagResource", "cloudwatch:UntagResource" (create, tag and delete the alarm)
    Each entry in double quotes followed by a comma, except the last one. Leave the other statements alone.
  6. Select Save changes. The editor may flag a few entries that were already there; they do not block saving. Reload and confirm your entries are present. The change applies at once to every account.

The list must still contain cloudfront:*, iam:*, route53:*, sts:* (GitHub's sign-in), cloudwatch:Describe*, Get*, List* and cloudtrail:LookupEvents; they were already there.

5GitHub login provider in IAM ONE TIMEWorkload account

This lets GitHub Actions sign in to AWS with a short-lived token instead of stored keys. An account can have only one provider for this URL, and other projects may share it.

Check first: IAM › Identity providers. If token.actions.githubusercontent.com is listed with audience sts.amazonaws.com, reuse it and only copy its ARN.
  1. Sign in to the workload account, open IAM, then Access management › Identity providers.
  2. If missing: Add provider › OpenID Connect, Provider URL https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com, Audience sts.amazonaws.com › Add provider.
  3. Open the provider and copy its ARN: arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:oidc-provider/token.actions.githubusercontent.com. It is not the deploy role ARN that Terraform prints later.

6Terraform state bucket ONE TIMEWorkload account

Terraform keeps its record of what it built (the state) in a private S3 bucket. It is separate from the website bucket and survives terraform destroy.

Check first: S3 › Buckets and your local terraform\environments\staging\backend.hcl. If the bucket named there exists, reuse it. Never create a second one for the same environment.
  1. Set the console region (top right) to United States (N. Virginia) us-east-1, open S3 › Buckets › Create bucket.
  2. General purpose, a globally unique name, ACLs disabled, Block all public access on, Bucket Versioning: Enable, encryption SSE-S3. Create.
  3. Open the bucket › Permissions › Bucket policy › Edit, paste the HTTPS-only policy below with your bucket name, Save changes.
  4. On your PC, copy backend.example.hcl to backend.hcl (only if it does not exist) and put your bucket name in it.
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Sid": "DenyInsecureTransport",
    "Effect": "Deny",
    "Principal": "*",
    "Action": "s3:*",
    "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::YOUR-STATE-BUCKET", "arn:aws:s3:::YOUR-STATE-BUCKET/*"],
    "Condition": { "Bool": { "aws:SecureTransport": "false" } }
  }]
}
# terraform\environments\staging\backend.hcl  (ignored by Git)
bucket = "YOUR-STATE-BUCKET"
key    = "one-step-at-a-time/staging/terraform.tfstate"
region = "us-east-1"

Shortcut: scripts\bootstrap-state.ps1 -Environment staging -Region us-east-1 -ExpectedAccountId "<account-id>" -WhatIf previews creating a bucket with the same settings and writes backend.hcl; run it again without -WhatIf. It refuses if backend.hcl already exists.

7Configure and create the site Your PCWorkload account

Needs the AWS CLI and Terraform 1.10 or later, below 2.0. First confirm which account the CLI uses:

aws sts get-caller-identity   # "Account" must be the workload account

Fill in site.tfvars

Check first: if terraform\environments\staging\site.tfvars exists, edit it; do not copy the example over it.
Copy-Item .\terraform\environments\staging\site.example.tfvars .\terraform\environments\staging\site.tfvars
SettingValueWatch out
aws_regionus-east-1
environmentstagingMust match the GitHub environment name.
site_bucket_nameGlobally unique, e.g. one-step-towards-ai-staging-site-<timestamp>No underscores; not the state bucket.
github_repositoryEasyLearnJava@6612328/one-step-towards-ai@1470924284GitHub puts IDs in its token for this repo. The plain owner/repo form fails. Other repos: open https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO, use owner.id and id.
github_oidc_provider_arnThe ARN from step 5Not the example 123456789012, and not the role ARN.
alert_emailA real mailbox you readNot replace@example.com, or alerts never arrive.

Plan, then apply EVERY CHANGE

Set-Location .\terraform\site
terraform init -reconfigure "-backend-config=..\environments\staging\backend.hcl"
terraform plan "-var-file=..\environments\staging\site.tfvars" "-out=staging.tfplan"
terraform show staging.tfplan      # first run: "15 to add"
terraform apply staging.tfplan     # CloudFront takes several minutes
terraform output                   # keep these four values

The 15 resources: website bucket + its 5 settings, CloudFront distribution + origin access control + headers policy, deploy role + its policy, health check, alarm, SNS topic, email subscription.

OutputLooks likeUsed for
website_urlhttps://d****.cloudfront.netGitHub WEBSITE_URL, and your browser
site_bucket_nameone-step-towards-ai-staging-site-****GitHub SITE_BUCKET
deploy_role_arnarn:aws:iam::****:role/one-step-staging-github-deployGitHub AWS_ROLE_ARN
aws_account_id****Check it is the workload account
Then confirm the alert email. AWS Notifications emails alert_email (check spam). Select Confirm subscription within 3 days, or later use SNS › Subscriptions › Request confirmation in us-east-1.
If an apply fails, read the error and fix the cause, then make a new plan. A saved plan cannot be applied twice.

8GitHub environment and deploy GitHub

The project lives in its own repository, EasyLearnJava/one-step-towards-ai; GitHub only runs workflows from .github/workflows at the repository root. Every push to main runs Checks (Terraform format and validate); it never touches AWS.

Create the staging environment ONE TIME

Check first: Settings › Environments. If staging exists, open it and only check the rule and variables.
  1. Repository Settings tab › Environments › New environment, name staging › Configure environment.
  2. Deployment branches and tags: change No restriction to Selected branches and tags.
  3. Add deployment branch or tag rule, Ref type Branch, pattern main › Add rule. It shows "1 branch and 0 tags allowed".
  4. Environment variables › Add environment variable for each row (environment, not repository variables):
VariableValue
AWS_REGIONus-east-1
SITE_BUCKEToutput site_bucket_name
WEBSITE_URLoutput website_url, no trailing slash
AWS_ROLE_ARNoutput deploy_role_arn
After a destroy and a new apply, the bucket name and CloudFront URL change. Update SITE_BUCKET and WEBSITE_URL before deploying again.

Deploy EVERY RELEASE

  1. Actions tab › Deploy website (left list) › Run workflow.
  2. Keep Use workflow from: main and environment staging › green Run workflow.
  3. The run signs in as the deploy role, uploads web/index.html, and passes only when the live page matches it. About 20 seconds.
  4. After pushing a fix, start a new run rather than Re-run jobs: a re-run reuses the old commit, and production only accepts a commit that already passed staging.
Deployments are manual. A push never changes the live site, and GitHub never runs terraform apply.

9Check it works EVERY RELEASEWorkload account, us-east-1

  1. Open website_url: the "One Step At A Time" page loads. Before the first deploy it returns 403 Forbidden; that is expected.
  2. CloudWatch › Alarms › All alarms: one-step-staging-unavailable is OK (a few minutes after the first deploy).
  3. SNS › Topics › one-step-staging-alerts › Subscriptions: your email is Confirmed.
  4. Opening the S3 bucket URL directly returns 403: only CloudFront can read it.
On our run: page HTTP 200 and identical to web/index.html, direct S3 403, alarm OK, email Confirmed. (The staging stack was destroyed afterwards on 25 Nov 2026, so there are no screenshots of these pages.)

10Errors we hit and the fixes

ErrorWhyFix
Your account must be verified before you can add new CloudFront resourcesNew-account holdSupport case (step 3), wait for Resolved, apply again.
sns:CreateTopic ... explicit deny in a service control policyRegion rule allowed only global services in us-east-1Add sns:* and the CloudWatch actions (step 4).
s3:CreateBucket ... explicit deny in a service control policySame rule; S3 was read-only in us-east-1Replace the s3: entries with s3:* (step 4).
Deploy: Could not assume role with OIDC: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity (run #1)github_oidc_provider_arn still had the example account 123456789012Put the real provider ARN in site.tfvars, new plan, apply.
MalformedPolicyDocument: Federated principals must be valid domain names or SAML metadata ARNsThe role ARN was pasted into github_oidc_provider_arnUse the oidc-provider/... ARN from step 5.
Same "Not authorized" again (run #2)GitHub sends repo:EasyLearnJava@6612328/one-step-towards-ai@1470924284:environment:staging, with IDs; the role expected the plain namegithub_repository in the ID form; variables.tf now accepts it (commit 356202b). New plan, apply, new run.
Alert subscription stuck at PendingConfirmationalert_email was replace@example.comReal email in site.tfvars, apply, click the confirmation email.
Billing page in the workload account asks you to sign in againThe bill lives in the management accountOpen billing from the management account (step 1, 2, 11).
git commit -m "..." in PowerShell breaks the message into file namesWindows PowerShell 5.1 splits arguments at inner double quotesWrite the message to a file and use git commit -F message.txt.

How we found the real GitHub subject

  1. Workload account, region us-east-1: CloudTrail › Event history.
  2. Lookup attribute Event name, value AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity. Failed attempts have no resource name.
  3. Open one: User name (and userIdentity.userName in the record) is the exact subject GitHub sent. The part between repo: and :environment: is what github_repository needs.

11Costs Management account

Look in Billing and Cost Management: Bills (month to date, Charges by account tab), Free Tier (usage against the free limits), Cost Explorer (filter Linked account). Figures update about once a day.

ItemPrice (AWS price list, us-east-1)
Route 53 health checkHTTPS and text matching are optional features: $1.00 each per month for AWS endpoints, $2.00 each for other endpoints. The basic check is free for the first 50 AWS-endpoint checks, otherwise $0.75.
CloudWatch alarm$0.10 per month; 10 alarms are always free.
CloudFront10 million requests and 1 TB out per month always free.
SNS email, S31,000 email notifications free; S3 a few cents.

About $2 to $6 a month while running, mostly the health check, all covered by the credits. Nothing is charged after terraform destroy except the tiny state bucket.

12Release checklist and clean up

Every release EVERY RELEASE

  1. Change web/index.html, commit, push to main; wait for Checks to pass.
  2. Actions › Deploy website › Run workflow › main + staging.
  3. Check the page, the alarm (OK) and that you still receive alerts.
  4. Infrastructure change (terraform/site/*.tf)? Plan and apply from your PC first.

Clean up Your PC

aws sts get-caller-identity
terraform state list
terraform plan -destroy "-var-file=..\environments\staging\site.tfvars" "-out=staging-destroy.tfplan"
terraform show staging-destroy.tfplan
terraform apply "staging-destroy.tfplan"   # deletes the site, all object versions too
Left behind on purpose: the state bucket, the OIDC provider, the SCP entries, the GitHub environment and its variables, and your payment method. Keep them for the next deploy; remove them only when no project needs them. After a new apply, update SITE_BUCKET and WEBSITE_URL in GitHub.
One project, every step, nothing secret on the page.
